91ibjt:2005: Best practices for implementing GPU virtualization on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod based on MIG technology by awschina on 20 Nov 2025 in Artificial Intelligence Permalink Share In today's rapidly evolving AI and machine learning landscape, GPU resources have become the core driver of enterprise digital transformation. However, traditional GPU usage patterns are facing unprecedented challenges: low resource utilization, persistently high costs, and increasing scheduling complexity. The advent of NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology provides a revolutionary solution to these pain points. This article will explore in depth how to deploy and manage MIG technology in an Amazon EKS environment to maximize GPU resource utilization. 1. Background: A New Era of GPU Resource Management 1.1 The Predicament of Traditional GPU Usage Patterns Before delving into MIG technology, we need to recognize the core challenges currently facing GPU resource management. In my years of cloud-native architecture practice, I have found that enterprises commonly suffer from the following problems in GPU resource usage: The "Matthew Effect" of Resource Utilization Traditional GPU scheduling models adopt a one-size-fits-all whole-card allocation strategy. A typical scenario: a lightweight inference task occupies an entire A100 GPU, yet actually uses less than 20% of its compute power and memory. This is like using a large truck to deliver a small parcel, resulting in enormous resource waste. According to our production environment statistics, the average GPU utilization in traditional models is only 30-40%, and peak utilization often does not exceed 60%. Geometric Growth of Cost Pressure High-end GPU prices are staggering. A single NVIDIA H200 has a market price exceeding $40,000, and the A100 is around $15,000. When enterprises need to build large-scale AI infrastructure, hardware investment often accounts for more than 70% of total costs. More concerning, due to low resource utilization, the actual unit computing cost is 2-3 times higher than the theoretical value. Exponential Growth in Scheduling Complexity Kubernetes' native GPU scheduler can only allocate resources in whole cards, which brings enormous challenges in multi-tenant environments. Different AI workloads have vastly different demands for GPU resources: lightweight inference may only need 2GB of memory, while large model training may require 80GB. Traditional schedulers cannot achieve fine-grained resource matching, leading to severe resource fragmentation. 1.2 MIG Technology: A Breakthrough in Hardware-Level Virtualization NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology represents a major breakthrough in the field of GPU virtualization. Unlike traditional software virtualization, MIG achieves true GPU partitioning at the hardware level, providing each instance with a fully isolated compute environment. Architectural Innovation MIG technology is based on the new design philosophy of the NVIDIA Ampere architecture. Each GPU is divided into multiple GPU Instances (GI), and each GI contains: Independent Streaming Multiprocessors (SM): dedicated compute units that ensure complete isolation of compute performance Dedicated memory partitions: hardware-level memory isolation that prevents memory conflicts between different instances Independent Copy Engines: dedicated data transfer engines that ensure consistent I/O performance Isolated codecs: independent video encoding/decoding units that support multimedia workloads This hardware-level partitioning design ensures that every MIG instance has predictable performance and is not affected by load changes on other instances. Flexible Configuration Strategy MIG technology supports multiple configuration modes that can be flexibly adjusted according to actual workload needs: A100 GPU configuration options: 5gb configuration: each instance has 1 GI and 5GB memory; 7 instances per card, suitable for lightweight inference 10gb configuration: each instance has 2 GIs and 10GB memory; 3 instances per card, suitable for medium-scale inference 20gb configuration: each instance has 3 GIs and 20GB memory; 2 instances per card, suitable for large model inference 40gb configuration: full GPU resources, suitable for large-scale training tasks H200 GPU configuration options: 18gb configuration: 7 instances, each with 18GB memory, supporting larger lightweight models 71gb configuration: 2 instances, each with 71GB memory, perfectly suited for 70B-parameter models 141gb configuration: full 141GB memory, supporting ultra-large-scale models 1.3 EKS Integration: Perfect Cloud-Native Fusion Combining MIG technology with Amazon EKS (managed Kubernetes service) not only solves the technical problems of GPU resource management, but also brings all the advantages of cloud-native architecture to enterprises. Intelligent Elastic Scaling In the EKS environment, MIG instances can be dynamically adjusted according to actual workload requirements. Through Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) and Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA), the system can automatically identify resource demand patterns and intelligently allocate MIG instances of appropriate specifications. This intelligent resource management mechanism can increase GPU utilization to over 85%. Unified Resource Management Experience Through the Kubernetes declarative API, developers can request MIG instances just as they request CPU and memory resources. This unified resource management model greatly reduces learning costs and improves development efficiency. At the same time, Kubernetes' resource quotas and limit mechanisms can also be seamlessly applied to MIG resources, enabling fine-grained resource governance.
